questions.question: During a new installation on equipment C16-01, where the latest approved drawing is available, the crew finds that conductor pulling tension does not match the approved information. What should the electrician do next?
options: Accept conductor pulling tension from appearance alone because similar equipment worked on a previous project.
Bypass the protective or verification step so the system can remain available while the cause is assumed.
Change several unrelated settings at once, then treat any temporary improvement as proof of the repair.
Pause, verify conductor pulling tension against approved information, resolve the discrepancy, document it, and then continue.
questions.explanation: Conductor pulling tension can directly affect damaged insulation, excessive pulling stress, moisture entry, poor support or loss of fire separation. The reliable approach is to use approved routing, conductor and raceway characteristics, pulling limits, support, environment, termination data and fire-separation requirements, make one controlled decision at a time, and preserve test and change records for independent review.
questions.sourceReference: MWA C, Task C-16, Sub-task C-16.01
questions.blueprintObjective: Apply conductor pulling tension knowledge while the electrician installs conductors and cables.

questions.question: During an intermittent fault investigation on equipment C16-03, where the work affects a critical operating load, while evaluating circuit voltage drop for work that installs raceways, a single-phase two-conductor circuit has a one-way length of 20 m, carries 21 A, and each conductor has 0.004 Ω/m resistance.
